item.title: Silicon Valley’s AI wunderkind launches Underdog, the most private Instinct/Muse competitor yet
item.description: Sigil Wen, backed by a Silicon Valley's who-who, has built an on-device AI assistant that promises to be free, fully private, and capable for everyday tasks.

item.title: Tesla’s Model 3 and Model Y can be a backup battery for your house
item.description: Some Tesla Model 3 and Model Y owners can use their EV battery to keep the lights on longer during a power outage, now that Tesla's expanding the Powershare Home Backup feature. item.title: How AI decision models could change content moderation
item.description: On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B, released with open weights.

item.title: Google’s power-hungry data centers crave nuclear energy
item.description: Google announced a new agreement to update six nuclear power plant sites across the US as the tech giant seeks to generate more electricity for its power-hungry data centers. item.description: Титаника убил айсберг. А ведь казалось, что он непотопляем. 1С, такая гигантская и непоколебимая, скоро легко может быть убита через ИИ. Вот первая ласточка уже прилетела от одного из программистов на 1С. Читать далее

item.title: AI computing startup Lambda to raise $4B ahead of planned IPO
item.description: Nvidia-backed Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation ahead of a planned 2027 IPO, led by Coatue and Blackstone.

item.title: Amazon’s last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is 30 percent off
item.description: Calling something “last-gen” usually means it comes with big compromises compared to the latest version. That’s not as true for the last-gen Kindle Paperwhite as it is with some other tech. item.title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
item.description: Personal AI agents promise to shop, book flights, and make reservations for you. But deliberate blocks and anti-bot defenses are getting in the way, leaving consumers caught in the middle. A new standard aims to help.
